meta.description: Booth quiz over the WCT GLP-1 study. Every question is a 'rank_barrier' — the visitor guesses which of two options patients raised more often, then sees the live count. Theme-based options are scored against themeCounts() in analysis.ts; keyword-based options against keyword_usage.json. leaderboard.votes are seeded conference-goer tallies — booth-session votes are added client-side from localStorage.
notes: rank_barrier options reference either theme/subtheme ids (codebook.json) or keyword ids (keyword_lexicon.json); the correct answer is whichever option's count is higher, resolved at load time — never hard-coded here.
domain.label names the competency a question probes; domain.wctEdge is the matching Worldwide Clinical Trials capability, surfaced in the results 'so-what'.
leaderboard.votes is a believable seed, not real telemetry; each question's counts sum to leaderboard.seed_players.

questions.prompt: Patients told us what would make a trial hard to join. Which came up more often?

options.label: The travel
options.sublabel: How far away the clinic is

domain.label: site logistics & travel burden
domain.wctEdge: decentralized trial design and site-network planning

questions.takeaway: Distance beat needles. Patients raised the drive to a site more than any blood draw — where you put a site matters more than which procedures you run.

questions.prompt: GLP-1 drugs are famous for their price. But across these interviews, which did patients raise more often?

domain.label: how patients weigh safety against cost

questions.takeaway: The sticker price gets the headlines, but worry about side effects came up even more often than cost — the bigger story in the room was safety, not money.

questions.prompt: Two GLP-1 drug families dominate the market. Which did patients name more often in these interviews?
questions.takeaway: Closer than you'd think. Ozempic and Wegovy own the headlines, but in these interviews patients named the two drug families almost evenly — tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) just edged it.

questions.prompt: What pulled patients toward joining a trial more strongly?
questions.takeaway: Altruism is real — but concrete support was raised nearly twice as often. Patients want to help; they also need the logistics solved.

questions.prompt: GLP-1 patients told us they want more education and support. Which did they ask for more often?

options.label: Help with the drug
options.sublabel: How the medication works & how to take it

questions.takeaway: Even on a medication that quiets appetite, the louder ask was for help with food — what to actually eat, how to plan meals. Nutrition guidance came up about twice as often as questions about the drug itself, and weight-loss patients say no one ever taught them this.

leaderboard.description: Seeded conference-goer tallies, keyed by question id then option key. Booth-session votes are added on top from localStorage.
